analytics.name: Analytic 1357
analytics.guidance: Detects anomalous use of COM, DDE, or named pipes for execution. Correlates creation or access of IPC mechanisms (e.g., named pipes, COM objects) with unusual parent-child process relationships or code injection patterns (e.g., Office spawning cmd.exe via DDE).

tuning.description: Environment-specific pipe names used legitimately vs anomalous (e.g., \\.\pipe\svcctl).
Expected parent-child process lineage to minimize false positives (e.g., explorer.exe spawning outlook.exe).

analytics.name: Analytic 1358
analytics.guidance: Detects abuse of UNIX domain sockets, pipes, or message queues for unauthorized code execution. Correlates unexpected socket creation with suspicious binaries, abnormal shell pipelines, or injected processes establishing IPC channels.

tuning.description: Expected UNIX socket paths used by system services and applications.
Legitimate processes expected to open pipes in shared directories.

log_sources.name: auditd:SYSCALL
log_sources.channel: socket: Suspicious creation of AF_UNIX sockets outside expected daemons

log_sources.name: auditd:SYSCALL
log_sources.channel: open: Access to named pipes or FIFO in /tmp or /dev/shm by unexpected processes

analytics.name: Analytic 1359
analytics.guidance: Detects anomalous use of Mach ports, Apple Events, or XPC services for inter-process execution or code injection. Focuses on unexpected processes attempting to send privileged Apple Events (e.g., automation scripts injecting into security-sensitive apps).

tuning.description: Whitelisted app-to-app Apple Event communications (e.g., Finder automation).
Baseline of Mach ports and XPC services normally used in the environment.

log_sources.name: macos:unifiedlog
log_sources.channel: Unusual Mach port registration or access attempts between unrelated processes

log_sources.name: macos:osquery
log_sources.channel: exec: Unexpected execution of osascript or AppleScript targeting sensitive apps
